fixtures.question: Explain caching versus persistent storage and their limitations.
fixtures.answer: Caching stores a reusable copy for fast access, while persistent storage retains authoritative data across restarts. A cache may lose entries or become stale and must not be treated as the only durable record. For example, after a service restarts it can rebuild a cache from its persistent database. Caching reduces repeated reads but adds invalidation complexity; persistent storage can be slower.
